headline: Streamlined ESRS finalised as CBAM downstream expansion talks advance
summary: The EU has finalised streamlined ESRS reporting standards ahead of mandatory reporting from 2027. Legislative negotiations are advancing on expanding CBAM to downstream finished products, which could impact imported power tools. Meanwhile, commercial battery passport schemes launched ahead of regulatory deadlines.

items.title: EU finalises streamlined ESRS ahead of November entry into force
items.what: The EU has finalised simplified European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) alongside a voluntary standard. Revised rules enter into force on 10 November 2026.
items.meaning: As your business falls under CSRD from financial year 2027, the streamlined standards define your direct disclosure requirements and scope of supplier data requests.
items.action: Review revised ESRS metrics to calibrate sustainability questionnaires for Chinese manufacturing suppliers.

items.title: Proposed CBAM expansion to downstream goods heads to trilogues
items.what: Legislative proposals to extend CBAM coverage to downstream finished products and counter circumventing practices are advancing towards EU trilogue negotiations.
items.meaning: While finished power tools currently avoid CBAM border carbon levies, an extension to downstream metal-containing products would capture your imported appliances.
items.action: Track trilogue negotiations on downstream product lists to model potential future border tax exposure.

items.title: Commercial Digital Battery Passport certification services launch
items.what: Testing bodies have begun launching commercial certification schemes for Digital Battery Passports, while electric mobility brands deploy compliant systems ahead of deadlines.
items.meaning: As the brand owner and manufacturer of your battery platform, you must establish data integration pipelines with cell suppliers in China.
items.action: Audit battery suppliers regarding material traceability and assess technical passport service providers.

items.title: Member states advance severe national penalties for EUDR
items.what: Germany and Ireland released national draft laws introducing steep turnover-linked fines and criminal sanctions for EUDR violations, alongside new EU customs codes.
items.meaning: Cardboard packaging and any wooden tool components imported into the EU must meet strict geolocation and due diligence rules from late December.
items.action: Ensure Chinese assembly partners can furnish geolocation data for packaging and timber materials.

items.title: EU enforcement begins against misleading environmental claims
items.what: Transposed rules banning generic environmental claims and uncertified sustainability labels under the Empowering Consumers Directive have started taking effect across member states.
items.meaning: Consumer-facing claims for power and garden tools must now be backed by verifiable data rather than general marketing terms.
items.action: Review packaging and website product copy to eliminate unsubstantiated environmental descriptors.
